# Context: elementwise-ops (op1, op2, cmp, bitwise, logical1, complex, where, cast, transmute, sub_dtype)

## Purpose

The concrete element-wise ops and their per-element kernels. Each op is a thin storage wrapper
(`define_op1!` op1.rs:159-257, `define_op2!` op2.rs:216-318) around `Op1<S,K>` (op1.rs:4-146) /
`Op2<S1,S2,K>` (op2.rs:5-203) whose zero-sized kernel calls a public scalar trait re-exported as
`jix::scalar::*` (e.g. `Div::div(a, b, &mut status)` + `div_bulk([T;N], .., simd)`). Traits and impls
are macro-generated by `scalar/traits_util.rs`; SIMD bodies go through `scalar/simd.rs` helpers on
top of `fearless_simd`. Execution happens in `storage/elementwise_pipeline.rs` (other subsystem) via
`read_as_elementwise_pipeline` -> `read_bulk::<N, CONTIGUOUS, S>`. Non-pipeline ops: `Where::read_data`
(own unsafe strided loops), `SubDtype` (struct-field view), `Transmute` (unsafe relabel of bytes).

## Contracts

Provided:
- P1. `f_bulk(xs)[i] == f(xs[i])` for every kernel (modulo NaN payload), and the OR of the statuses
  is the same. Bulk is SIMD only where an impl gives `fn f_bulk = |v| ...` (traits_util.rs:101-143,
  279-328); otherwise the trait default loops the scalar fn (traits_util.rs:16-34, 175-195). A
  status-taking trait with a status-less bulk body does not compile, so status drop is not silent.
- P2. Kernels never panic on data: they write a fallback value and OR an `ArithmeticErrorKind` bit
  (error.rs:269-282, 387-419; contract text elementwise_pipeline.rs:49-51). The pipeline ORs the
  per-chunk status and calls `ReadContext::check_op_status` once per `to_buf`, AFTER the output is
  fully written (elementwise_pipeline.rs:245-310, codec/mod.rs:440-447). Defaults: DivideByZero and
  InvalidOperation = Error, Overflow and Underflow = Warn (error.rs:359-367). No kernel sets Underflow.
- P3. Output dtype is `K::Output::DTYPE` (op1.rs:129-131, op2.rs:186-188); zero-size output dtypes are
  rejected at construction (op1.rs:34, op2.rs:40, sub_dtype.rs:93).
- P4. Shapes must be exactly equal: Op2 (op2.rs:41-53), Clamp (cmp.rs:739-746), Where
  (where_op.rs:88-96). No broadcasting in Rust ops: callers pass 0-stride Broadcast views (jix-py
  does it in jix-py/src/ops/common/broadcast.rs). Operator impls / `Array::<op>()` methods `.unwrap()`
  with `#[track_caller]` and panic on mismatch (documented e.g. where_op.rs:6-9).
- P5. No implicit dtype promotion on the Rust side; an op exists only for implemented (lhs, rhs)
  pairs. Same-type only: Add/Sub/Mul/Div/Divide*/Remainder*/cmp/Maximum/Minimum/bit and/or/xor.
  Mixed: Pow int x {u8,u16,u32,i8,i16,i32,i64}, f32|f64 x {i8,u8,i16,u16,i32}, f32|f64 x f32,
  f64 x f64, f16 x {i8,u8,i16,u16,i32,f16} (op2.rs:1168-1229); Shl/Shr any int x any int, output =
  lhs type (bitwise.rs:97-125, 287-293); Rotate int x u32 (bitwise.rs:265-274). Promotion lives in
  jix-py (jix-py/src/ops/common/dtype_promote.rs, dispatch.rs).
- P6. `Where`: numpy.where semantics, condition dtype bool, `x.dtype() == y.dtype()` runtime-checked
  (where_op.rs:74-96). `Transmute`: ONLY itemsize equality is checked (transmute.rs:86-98). `SubDtype`:
  pull mode returns the parent buffer shifted by the field offset with the parent's strides
  (sub_dtype.rs:131-136); push mode copies field bytes with NdCopier (sub_dtype.rs:138-163).

Relied on:
- R1. `check_dtype(T, K::Output)` (error.rs:154-167; Dtype eq dtype.rs:914-941) + a const size assert
  justify `transmute_copy::<[K::Output;N],[T;N]>` (op1.rs:73+110-112, op2.rs:122+165-167,
  cmp.rs:806+860-862). Sound only because Dtype equality => identical layout/validity, which rests on
  the `unsafe trait Dtyped` impls (dtype.rs:1147-1155).
- R2. `read_bulk` safety (elementwise_pipeline.rs:53-63): the caller (`to_buf`, inner_loop_impl
  elementwise_pipeline.rs:591-651) guarantees elements `offset..offset+N` are in bounds for every leaf
  and, when REQUIRE_ALIGNED, aligned; `CONTIGUOUS` promises inner stride == itemsize. Nodes here just
  forward the same `offset`/`status` (op1.rs:104-107, op2.rs:161-162, cmp.rs:855-857, where_op.rs:396-401).
- R3. A child's `read_data(index, ctx, None)` returns a buffer valid for the whole `index` region with
  one stride per dim (core_trait.rs:71-107). `StridedBuf` carries no shape (buf.rs:44-48), so `Where`
  and `SubDtype` trust it blindly. `ArrayStorage` is a SAFE public trait (core_trait.rs:56) and
  `Array::from_storage` is safe (array.rs:1601): a safe user impl can lie (forward another storage's
  buffer, wrong dtype, unstable shape). Library-wide trust boundary - report once, not per op.
- R4. `bool` bytes are 0 or 1. Read as typed `bool` with no check in Where (where_op.rs:277-283, 305,
  331), pipeline leaves (`OperandTyped` elementwise_pipeline.rs:821-858) and every bool kernel.
  Established for bools produced here (cmp/IsNan/cast-to-bool: simd.rs:375-383 maps -1/0 to 0/1).
  NOT established (that I found): archive load of a bool dtype (no validation in jix/src/archive),
  `Transmute` to bool (caller's unsafe contract), jix-py zero-copy numpy bool views (numpy allows
  bytes other than 0/1 via `.view(bool)`).
- R5. Struct dtype invariants (fields in bounds, aligned or packed layout; dtype.rs:459-529, 578-717).
  SubDtype uses them with no re-check (sub_dtype.rs:135, 149). Packed structs place fields at
  offsets that are not multiples of the field alignment -> SubDtype pull output is misaligned, which
  is allowed: no StridedBuf is promised aligned (core_trait.rs:97-101, buf.rs:20-22).
- R6. `NdIterUnordered` (util/nd_iter_unordered.rs:32-200) yields in-bounds per-operand offsets and
  correct `is_contiguous`/`is_strides_aligned`; empty region -> visits nothing (line 78), all-size-1
  -> one element (line 85).
- R7. `REQUIRE_ALIGNED` is false on x86/x86_64/aarch64 (util/mod.rs:641-645): typed reads there are
  `read_unaligned`, so alignment bugs only bite on other targets (wasm, riscv, ...).
- R8. fearless_simd 1.1.0 semantics (~/.cargo/registry/src/*/fearless_simd-1.1.0): integer
  neg/abs/mul wrap (fallback uses wrapping_*), `truncate_from_precise` saturates with NaN->0,
  `saturating_narrow` is signed/unsigned per type, int `narrow` truncates, f64->f32 `narrow` is a
  rounding convert, `mul_add_precise` is fused on every level.

Unsafe-fn preconditions and who establishes them:
- `Transmute::new`/`new_array` (transmute.rs:86, 105), `Array::transmute_elements`/`_dyn`
  (transmute.rs:14, 28): CALLER guarantees every element is a valid bit pattern of the new dtype.
  Int/float targets: any initialized bytes. bool targets (or struct fields of bool): bytes 0/1. Struct
  SOURCE with padding read as ints/`[u8;N]`: padding must be initialized (uninit padding from a Plain
  over Rust structs would be UB; decompressed Compact bytes are initialized). Target padding: don't-care.
  `_dyn` panics (unwrap, not UB) on itemsize mismatch; no `# Panics` doc.
- `read_bulk` (pub(crate) trait method): see R2, established by elementwise_pipeline.rs.
- `OperandTyped::new_input` (elementwise_pipeline.rs:808-818): data is a valid view of `dtype` and
  `dtype == T::DTYPE`; established by `check_dtype` in the default pipeline (core_trait.rs:132-134).
- Where inner loops (where_op.rs:248, 317): `len` elements at the given strides in bounds of out/x,
  y and cond; out and y distinct allocations; `itemsize == size_of::<T>()` (hard assert 262).

## Unsafe inventory

- op1.rs:98-113, op2.rs:155-168, cmp.rs:849-863: forward `read_bulk` (R2) + `transmute_copy` (R1).
  Local: check_dtype in the outer fn, const size assert. Non-local: Dtyped impl correctness.
- op2.rs:181 `assert_unchecked_eq!(a.shape(), b.shape())`: established ONCE in `Op2::new`
  (op2.rs:41-53, also via cmp.rs:435 swapped). Relies on both children's `shape()` never changing -
  non-local, any ArrayStorage impl (R3). Debug builds only debug_assert.
- where_op.rs:200-245: table of `unsafe fn` inner loops called per inner run with NdIterUnordered
  offsets (R6) over: out (materialize_out_buf or caller's), y_view and condition_view (pull views).
  In-bounds relies on R3+R6. Loop choice by (itemsize, alignment) at where_op.rs:216-225; `aligned` is
  trivially true when !REQUIRE_ALIGNED (192-197); contiguity checks are debug_assert only (257-261).
- where_op.rs:267-312 typed loop: reads `[T; LANES]` of x/y and `[bool; LANES]` of cond (R4), writes x.
- where_op.rs:329-338 generic loop: `copy_from_nonoverlapping(y -> out, itemsize)` where !cond;
  distinctness holds because out is a fresh pool buffer or the caller's `&mut` (cannot alias a shared
  view without the caller's own unsafe).
- where_op.rs:390-403 pipeline: forwards read_bulk; condition read as bool (R4).
- sub_dtype.rs:135 `with_offset` (buf.rs:248-259): actually bounds-checked slicing (panic, not UB);
  validity of the shifted view for the parent strides relies on R5.
- sub_dtype.rs:149 `get_unchecked(offset..)`: UB if offset > len. Established only because the read is
  non-empty (130, 145) so the buffer holds >= 1 parent element of itemsize >= offset + field size (R5).
- sub_dtype.rs:153-162 `NdCopier::copy` with parent strides, out strides, field itemsize (R3, R5).
- transmute.rs:14-30, 86-107: unsafe API surface only; no internal unsafe operations.
- None in cast.rs, bitwise.rs, logical1.rs, complex.rs, scalar/simd.rs, scalar/traits_util.rs.

## Edge-case surface

Integers:
- Add/Sub/Mul/Square/Neg/Abs wrap with NO status (op2.rs:576-637, op1.rs:342-397, 448-453).
- Div/DivideTrunc/Floor/Euclid: b==0 -> 0 + DivideByZero; MIN/-1 -> MIN + Overflow (`int_quotient`
  op2.rs:711-733). Remainder*: b==0 -> 0 + DivideByZero; MIN % -1 -> 0, NO error (`checked_rem*`
  returns None for both; `int_remainder` op2.rs:735-750 flags only b==0). Signed floor/euclid
  adjustments use non-wrapping `+`/`-` (op2.rs:655, 672, 694) - debug-overflow if ever reachable.
- Pow: b<0 -> 0 + InvalidOperation (also for base 1/-1); b > u32::MAX via square-and-multiply loop
  (op2.rs:1182-1190); u8/u16/u32 exponents via `b as u32`.
- Shifts: `shift_count` reinterprets negative counts unsigned -> past every width (bitwise.rs:295-313)
  -> 0, or -1 for negative signed Shr. SIMD i32 Shr clamps count to 31 (110-115); u32 Shr selects 0
  for counts >= 32 (116-125). Rotates take the count mod width.
Floats (f32/f64):
- NaN: Maximum/Minimum -> canonical `Self::NAN` (cmp.rs:50-58, 104-112); comparisons false (`!=` true);
  ApproxEq false; cast to int -> 0; cast to bool -> true; Sign(NaN) = NaN.
- -0.0: Sign -> 0.0; Sqrt(-0.0) = -0.0 no error; Max/Min of +-0 may return either; div/rem results use
  copysign (op2.rs:826, 893); RemainderFloor zero result takes b's sign (op2.rs:854-858, 934).
- inf: div_rem_trunc specials (op2.rs:819-827): inf dividend -> NaN quotient; x/0 -> +-inf; 0/0 NaN;
  inf/0 -> inf with NO error (dividend not finite). `float_div_error` (op2.rs:1138-1149) vs SIMD
  `quotient_v` (959-979) must classify identically; remainders only flag InvalidOperation (982-1002).
- EXACT_LIMIT 2^24 / 2^53 (op2.rs:1084-1095): `rem_trunc` switches to `a % b` past it (836-839,
  902-919); quotients are "within one ulp" past it (doc 811-813).
- Pow floats (`float_pow_error` op2.rs:1244-1256), evaluated only when the result is non-finite and no
  operand is NaN: DivideByZero iff base == 0 and exp < 0; Overflow iff inf result, finite operands,
  base != 0; InvalidOperation iff NaN result.
- op1 float errors via `float_op1!` (op1.rs:507-558): condition tested in T, then re-tested in f64 in a
  cold fn; Exp overflow only for finite x; Ln(+-0) DivideByZero; Asin/Acos |x| > 1; trig of inf.
f16 (feature `half`): computed in f32 and rounded once (op2.rs:598-611, op1.rs:398-413) - for + - * /
  sqrt this is correctly rounded (24 >= 2*11+2 bits), NOT a double-rounding bug. Error checks use the
  f16-rounded result (op1.rs:531-545, op2.rs:1123-1137, 1210-1229). No SIMD bodies for f16. Casts INTO
  f16 go through `as f32` (cast.rs:59) - see Suspicions.
Complex (feature `num-complex`): only Complex<f32>/<f64> are Dtyped (dtype.rs:1181-1183), so the
  Complex<f16> impls (op1.rs:420-425, 466-471; op2.rs:618-623, 783-788; cmp.rs:170-176; cast.rs:303-304)
  are unreachable from Array ops. Div is num_complex's naive formula with no status (op2.rs:376,
  777-782): overflows for |b| > sqrt(MAX). Abs uses hypot, output real (op1.rs:354-367). Complex ->
  bool is `!= 0+0i` (cast.rs:295-300); complex cannot cast to real. ApproxEq per component (cmp.rs:330-348).
bool: cmp via formulas (cmp.rs:191, 210, 229 `!a & b`, 243 `!a | b`); bitwise via & | ^ !; cast
  bool->X via `as i8` (cast.rs:55). Any non-0/1 byte = UB (R4).
Struct dtypes / inner shape: only Where, Transmute and SubDtype accept them. Where uses typed fast loops
  for (itemsize, align) in {(1,1),(2,2),(4,2),(4,4),(8,4),(8,8),(16,8|16)}, else a byte copy loop.
  SubDtype rejects parents with an inner shape (sub_dtype.rs:78-82); the field may have one.
Empty / 0-d: pipeline returns early on a 0-length dim (elementwise_pipeline.rs:209-211); Where relies on
  NdIterUnordered::empty; SubDtype has explicit empty paths (sub_dtype.rs:130-147).
Broadcast: 0-stride inputs may be staged (elementwise_pipeline.rs:488-499); in pull mode the output gets
  stride 0 on dims where every input is 0-stride (pick_output_layout 885-941). Where does no staging.
SIMD/scalar split - the same element can go through either path:
- contiguous runs: runtime level, LANES = 4|8 vectors' worth (elementwise_pipeline.rs:664-697);
  strided runs: compile-time baseline level, LANES <= 4; the tail of every run: N=1 (scalar).
- map_vectors* fall back to scalar unless N is a multiple of the vector chunk (simd.rs:183-185,
  225-230); bool-output SIMD only on AVX2 (simd.rs:363); casts gate on `only_on` levels (cast.rs:79-82).
  So any SIMD/scalar disagreement shows up as position-, length-, stride- or CPU-dependent results.

## Intentional behaviors

- Integer wrap on add/sub/mul/neg/abs/square/pow, no Overflow flag (op2.rs:334, 345, 356, 1155;
  op1.rs:327-328, 374, 430-431). `-i8::MIN == i8::MIN` (doc op1.rs:720 says "in release builds" but the
  kernel always wraps - doc nit).
- Integer div/rem by zero -> 0 with DivideByZero; MIN/-1 -> MIN with Overflow; MIN % -1 -> 0, no error
  (op2.rs:368-370, 387-389, 488-489; Python tests jix-py/python/tests/test_errstate.py:21-49).
- Reads FAIL by default on DivideByZero / InvalidOperation (unlike numpy's warn); Overflow warns
  (error.rs:359-367; test_errstate.py:20). Underflow never reported (op1.rs:619).
- Float DivideTrunc/Floor/Euclid use the EXACT quotient, not rounded a/b (`1.0 // 0.1 == 9`;
  op2.rs:390-392, 433-434, 461-462); infinite dividend -> NaN like numpy floor_divide (op2.rs:812-813).
  RemainderFloor is CPython float `%` (zero takes b's sign, op2.rs:527, 850-859).
- Complex Div reports no errors yet (op2.rs:376).
- Pow: negative int exponent -> 0 + InvalidOperation (op2.rs:1155-1156); float rules (1158-1161).
- Round is half-away-from-zero, not numpy's half-to-even (op1.rs:607-609). Sign(+-0.0) = 0.0
  (op1.rs:281-282). Sqrt(-0.0) = -0.0 no error (op1.rs:580). Exp overflow only for finite x (618-619).
- Maximum/Minimum propagate NaN as the canonical NaN (not the operand's) and may return either zero
  (cmp.rs:24-29, 78-83). Clamp = minimum(maximum(a, lo), hi), so lo > hi gives hi (cmp.rs:700-705).
- ApproxEq is NOT numpy.isclose: `|a-b| <= max(atol, rtol*max(|a|,|b|))`, same-sign infs equal
  (cmp.rs:905-908, 939-943).
- Shifts by >= width or negative -> 0 / -1 (bitwise.rs:89-91, 279-281); rotates mod width (248, 259).
- Casts follow Rust `as`: float->int saturates, NaN -> 0; int->int truncates/wraps; X->bool is `!= 0`
  (NaN -> true); bool -> 0/1 (cast.rs:9-18, 55-60; tests cast.rs:657-658). Casts never set a status
  (CastKernel ignores it, cast.rs:408-420). i64/u64 -> f32 SIMD deliberately disabled (double rounding,
  cast.rs:213, 245).
- Transmute checks only itemsize; alignment may differ (transmute.rs:40-42).
- Where evaluates BOTH branches for every element (where_op.rs:165-175, 396-402): an error in the
  unselected branch (e.g. `where(b != 0, a / b, 0)`) still fails the read by default. Eager like numpy;
  undocumented - treat as design unless you find docs saying otherwise.
- Doc nits, not bugs: SwapBytes says i8/u8 unsupported but they are implemented (bitwise.rs:224-225 vs
  171-175); `fixed_lhs_type` actually fixes the RHS item type (common.rs:29-40); Cast docs list only
  Complex<f32>/<f64> (cast.rs:366).

## Hot spots

- SIMD vs scalar equality. Most SIMD tests compare with `==` via `same_value` (util/test_util.rs:1357-
  1372): -0.0 == +0.0 passes, so signed-zero divergence in Neg/Floor/Ceil/Sqrt/Abs/Square/Add/Sub/Mul/
  Div/casts is untested; only the div/rem family is bit-exact (op2.rs:1705-1760). Test inputs are 64
  fixed values (test_util.rs:1305-1350): no mid-range values (e.g. 200.0 for f32->u8, 40000.0 for
  f32->u16), and only levels the CI CPU has (AVX-512/NEON paths likely untested). Concrete
  array tests are tiny (< LANES elements) so they hit only the scalar tail.
- Status equality scalar vs SIMD is tested only for Sqrt and the float div/rem family
  (op1.rs:1673-1707, op2.rs:2908-2961). Does `quotient_v` agree with `float_div_error` for b NaN, a inf,
  -0.0 divisors, results that become inf only after `div - 1.0`?
- Integer division family per signedness and width (op2.rs:639-763): MIN/-1 and zero in every op; can
  `d + (...)` (655), `d - (...)` (672), `rem + b` (694) overflow? (I believe not; prove or break it.)
- Float div/rem past EXACT_LIMIT: `div_floor` decides its adjustment from the inexact residual while
  `rem_floor` uses fmod; can `a == q*b + r` (up to rounding) or sign rules break between the pair?
- Pow classification uses `b as Self` / `b as f32` and `powi(b as i32)` (op2.rs:1196-1229): any exponent
  type where the cast changes the value used for the error test (e.g. u16 -> i32 fine, i32 -> f32 lossy)?
- Cast step chains (cast.rs:184-271): KT/KU vector counts, widen-then-bitcast for sign extension
  (i8 -> u16 must sign-extend), truncate vs saturating narrow for float->int, `only_on` lists vs the
  levels the fearless_simd op is actually correct on. Scalar table cast.rs:55-60 (f16, bool, complex).
- Shr SIMD (bitwise.rs:110-125): i32 rhs bitcast to u32 then `min(31)`; u32 rhs `select`; does every
  (lhs, rhs) signedness pair match `unbounded_shr(shift_count(b))`?
- Bool-output SIMD (simd.rs:299-384): mask narrowing order for 16/32/64-bit lanes on AVX2.
- Where::read_data (where_op.rs:153-342): strides of three differently laid-out buffers, 0-stride
  broadcast cond/y, push-mode out with caller strides, typed-loop table, empty/0-d regions.
- SubDtype pull mode (sub_dtype.rs:126-136): the returned view keeps the PARENT strides and is shifted
  by the field offset - is it valid for every consumer that assumes nothing more than R3? Push-mode
  `get_unchecked` (149). Interaction with TypeDyn / element_type_change (182-190).
- Recent churn: 98b2ed3 (#81 kernel errors; rewrote traits_util.rs, simd.rs, most of op1/op2),
  d45957f (#77 divide/remainder floor/trunc/euclid + Clamp), 02ba65d (#82 f16 Pow), ce96bfd (#80 x*x
  shortcut, jix-py only), bb1ee2c (#84 where/stack promotion, jix-py side).

### Suspicions (unverified)

- cast.rs:59 (used for f64 -> f16 and, via cast.rs:280-281, Complex<f64> -> Complex<f16>):
  `f16::from_f32(value as f32)` double-rounds f64 sources. 1 + 2^-11 + 2^-40 should round to
  1 + 2^-10 but f32 lands exactly on the f16 tie and ties-to-even gives 1.0. The test oracle
  (cast.rs:540-547) uses the same formula; `half::f16::from_f64` rounds directly. Int sources are fine
  (exact in f32 throughout f16's finite range).
- op2.rs:181: `assert_unchecked_eq!` on child shapes trusts `shape()` to be stable forever; with a safe
  user `ArrayStorage` whose shape() changes, safe code reaches UB (same pattern ops/into_type.rs:87,102).
- jix-py/src/ops/op2.rs:681-688 (cross-subsystem): `jix.power(x, 0.5)` routes to Sqrt: x = -inf gives
  NaN + InvalidOperation (raises by default) where np.power gives +inf, and x = -0.0 gives -0.0 vs
  +0.0. `power(x, 2)` routes to Square, which drops the Overflow flag the Pow kernel would set.
- Bool validity (cross-subsystem): no 0/1 validation found on archive load or for numpy bool inputs;
  any bool consumer here (Where, Not/And/Or/Xor, cmp, cast from bool) then reads an invalid bool.
